root_causes.evidence: The reconciliation session held a write lock on the ledger. Payments logged 'database is locked' write failures and ledger write_errors kept climbing. After release_lock, write_errors fell to 0.

Payments 1.5 was deployed just before the failures. After the lock release it still failed with response_unavailable (about 87% errors, p95 about 1200 ms) and duplicate payments rose from 14 to 86. After rolling back to 1.3: error rate 0, p95 47 ms, duplicates steady at 86, and the probe passes end to end.

actions.reason: Payments errors are 'database is locked', caused by the reconciliation session holding a write lock on the ledger, so release that lock first.

The lock errors stopped after the release, but payments keeps failing with response_unavailable and duplicate payments are still climbing. That points to the 1.5 release deployed just before the incident, so roll payments back.

escalation.reason: The system is healthy and duplicate payments have stopped at 86 on release 1.3. Those 86 duplicates in the ledger need a person to review, since I may not reverse money, so I will escalate before declaring done.
escalation.ask: Payments release 1.5, deployed and now rolled back to 1.3, created 86 duplicate payments in the ledger. The count is stable at 86 after the rollback. Finance and operations must review and remediate these duplicates through the proper process; the incident commander has not moved or reversed any money. The reconciliation batch was rolled back when its lock was released. Rerun it once the duplicates are handled, outside peak hours, so it does not block ledger writes. Also find out why reconciliation held a long write lock during live traffic.

sbar.situation: Payments and the gateway are back to baseline after the incident commander released a ledger lock and rolled payments back from 1.5 to 1.3; recovery was confirmed with two clean checks in a row, the last at 59 s. The 86 duplicate payments created by release 1.5 are escalated to the on-call engineer for the ledger.
sbar.background: Payments release 1.5 was deployed just before failures began. At the same time, the reconciliation session held a write lock on the ledger, so payments logged 'database is locked' write failures and ledger write_errors kept climbing.
sbar.assessment: The incident commander ended the reconciliation session's lock on the ledger (confidence 0.9), and ledger write_errors fell to 0, but payments 1.5 still failed with response_unavailable at about 87% errors and p95 about 1200 ms while duplicates rose from 14 to 86. The incident commander then rolled payments back from 1.5 to 1.3 (confidence 0.85): error rate is 0, p95 is 47 ms, duplicates are steady at 86, and the payment probe passes end to end.
sbar.recommendation: Finance and operations must review and remediate the 86 duplicate ledger payments through the proper process; the incident commander has not moved or reversed any money. The reconciliation batch was rolled back when its lock was released, so rerun it outside peak hours once the duplicates are handled. Find out why reconciliation held a long write lock during live traffic, and keep payments 1.5 off until its duplicate-payment fault is fixed.
